content.hook_text: I used to think faith meant having all the answers.
content.verse_text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight.
content.misconception: I thought trusting God meant figuring out His plan first — mapping every step, analyzing every decision, needing certainty before I moved. If I couldn't explain it, I couldn't obey it.
content.actual_meaning: But 'lean not on your own understanding' isn't an invitation to stop thinking — it's a call to stop demanding understanding as a prerequisite for trust. The Hebrew word for 'trust' (batach) implies throwing yourself down on a bed — a posture of total reliance, not intellectual agreement. God says: move first, clarity often comes later.
content.cta: What's something you're waiting to understand before you trust?
content.caption:
I used to think faith meant having all the answers. Turns out it mostly means being okay with not having them — and choosing to trust anyway.

This verse hit different when I stopped reading it as advice and started reading it as permission. Permission to not have it figured out. Permission to take the next step scared. Permission to let God be God while I just... be human.

What's something you're waiting to understand before you trust? Drop it below. Let's be confused together. 👇
